chunks: Abu Kurayb and Abu Sa‘id al-Ashajj narrated to me; they said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father Idris ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Awdi, who said:

When al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was killed, the people wanted to have horses trample him. Fiddah said to Zaynab, ‘My lady, Safinah had once been shipwrecked at sea and came out to an island, where he encountered a lion. He said, “O Abu al-Harith, I am the mawla of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).” So it growled before him until it stationed him upon the road, while the lion remained crouching to one side. So let me go to it and inform it of what they are going to do tomorrow.’

He said: So she went to it and said, ‘O Abu al-Harith.’ It raised its head. Then she said, ‘Do you know what they intend to do tomorrow to Abu ‘Abd Allah (عليه السلام)? They intend to have horses trample his back.’

He said: So it walked until it placed its forelegs upon the body of al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then the horses approached, but when they saw it, ‘Umar ibn Sa‘d, may Allah curse him, said to them: ‘It is a disturbance; do not stir it up. Turn back.’ So they turned back.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَارِثِ: A kunyah used here to address the lion
key_terms.أَسَدٍ: A lion, presented here as intervening at the body of al-Husayn (عليه السلام)
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ: Imam al-Husayn (عليه السلام), the martyred grandson of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم)
key_terms.جَسَدِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The body of al-Husayn (عليه السلام) after his martyrdom
key_terms.زَيْنَبَ: Zaynab, the noble lady addressed in the report
key_terms.فِتْنَةٌ: A disturbance or turmoil to be avoided
key_terms.فِضَّةُ: Fiddah, the attendant associated with the household of Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.مَوْلَى: A devoted servant or affiliated client; here, one belonging to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم)

ai.seo_question: How was the body of al-Husayn (عليه السلام) protected after Karbala according to this narration?
ai.summary: This report narrates an event after the martyrdom of al-Husayn (عليه السلام), when an attempt to desecrate his body was thwarted through the intervention of a lion. It highlights the sanctity and honor of al-Husayn (عليه السلام) and reflects the extraordinary signs associated with the tragedy of Karbala in Shia tradition.

en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Yunus from Masqala al-Tahhan who has said the following.

“I heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say, ‘When al-Husayn was murdered his wife who was from the tribe of al-Kalb began to organize a mourning gathering. She wept and the ladies and servants wept until their tears dried up. There was one female servant (slave) who would weep and her tears would not stop. She called her and said, “How is it that our tears have dried up and your tears have not?” She said, “When I suffer I drink Sawiq, (a kind of soup made of wheat and or barley).” She then ordered to prepare Sawiq and food. She drink and eat and give others to drink and eat and would say, “We find energy to weep for al-Husayn.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Certain birds were given to al-Kalbia lady to help her in her mourning for al-Husayn (a.s.). When she saw them she asked, “What are these?” They told her that they were a gift to help her in mourning for al-Husayn (a.s.).” She said, “We are not in a wedding. What do we do with them?” She told her servants to take them out of the house. When they were taken out of the house they just disappeared as if they did not exist or flew between the heavens and earth and afterwards no trace of them were found in the house.”
